Anya (sec): Heads-up — during the daily canary we saw a signing failure for the new compact base image. Looks like RBAC change last night removed the build service account's encryption/decryption role on the KMS key. Filing here so we can coordinate rollback or mitigation.
Devon (eng-infra): ack, checking RBAC audit now. I pushed a change to tighten perms yesterday, probably the culprit.
James (eng-runtime): what error are we seeing?
Anya (sec): sec-bot posted the error in the ticket, copying snippet here:```
ERROR: cosign: failed to upload signature: rpc error: code = PermissionDenied desc = rpc: request did not have the required permission kms.cryptoKeys.encrypt```
Devon (eng-infra): yep that's KMS encrypt denied — build pipeline signs with cosign using the repo key. I can re-add kms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter to the build-sa for the specific key.
Maria (sre): before granting wide perms, can we bind only to the key resource? try `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` scoped at the key instead of project.
Anya (sec): agreed. Also we need audit logs for the failed calls to validate whether it was attempted from the expected runner. Last 24h show 3 failed sign attempts.
Devon (eng-infra): fetching audit entries now. If callers are from `ci-runner-5`, we might have a stale SA used by the canary.
sec-bot: [automated] KMS access denied events (3) detected for key projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/repo/cryptoKeys/signing-key. First seen 1717879201.
James (eng-runtime): quick question — the runtime uses cached images and we have a KV cache in front of signing metadata. Could a cached manifest cause an invalid signature attempt?
Anya (sec): unlikely for KMS deny. The attempt reaches KMS. But good to check manifest lineage.
Devon (eng-infra): audit shows two attempts from `ci-runner-5` and one from `canary-runner`. Runner ip range matches expected. The SA attached to ci-runner-5 lost the key-binding in the policy diff: ```- members: serviceAccount:build-sa@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com
  role: roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter```
Maria (sre): rollback option: reapply the binding, run a signed canary (non-prod key) then do a staged roll for prod. Can we do a quick hotfix granting minimal permission to the key ring?
Anya (sec): hotfix fine, but add an audit entry and TTL on the ephemeral grant. Who can apply?
Devon (eng-infra): I can reapply now with a conditional TTL via iam-conditions? Cloud IAM condition can set `request.time < timestamp("2024-05-08T01:30:00Z")` style, but our infra tooling doesn't support ephemeral TTLs yet. I can add and annotate for manual revoke.
James (eng-runtime): if we re-grant, we should also gate the build with a canary label so the signing key sees only canary traffic first. We'll run `cosign sign --key gcpkms://projects/.../cryptoKeys/signing-key --annotations canary=true` in canary job.
Anya (sec): good. Also add to the runbook: who approves emergency key grants, Slack incident channel, and how to revoke. We need audit-log forwarding to SIEM so compliance can see the grant.
Maria (sre): I'll open an incident channel `#inc-image-signing` and add the runbook checklist. Action items: 1) Devon reapply key-binding with minimal scope (in 5m). 2) Devon add comment to PR explaining reason. 3) James run signed canary and post results. 4) Anya update runbook and add TTL step.
Devon (eng-infra): doing step 1 now. Reapplying scoped role to `projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/repo/cryptoKeys/signing-key` for `build-sa`.
sec-bot: [automated] IAM policy change: role roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter added for serviceAccount:build-sa@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com by devon at 1717879805
Devon (eng-infra): done. Please note I left a comment in infra PR: "temporary restoration of KMS encrypter role; follow-up to remove extraneous perms after canary."
James (eng-runtime): kicked off canary sign job. First run shows success: `cosign: signature upload OK`
Maria (sre): monitoring — make sure this is visible in Redwood Console tracing so we can tag the request path.
Anya (sec): confirm SIEM got the events?
sec-bot: [automated] Forwarded 3 KMS audit events to splunk: index=security sourcetype=gcp:kms at 1717879902
Anya (sec): good. Next steps: 1) convert this into a short postmortem entry (no customer impact). 2) add a preflight check in build pipeline to assert KMS roles present before attempting sign. 3) schedule a follow-up to add ephemeral credential automation for key grants.
Devon (eng-infra): I'll open a PR for preflight check: small script `verify_kms_bindings.sh` that queries the key IAM and fails fast if binding missing.
James (eng-runtime): I'll add a canary flag and have the runtime treat `canary=true` annotations as signal to not propagate to production trace.
Maria (sre): propose we add an alert: >1 KMS PERMISSION_DENIED within 30m -> create pager or at least Slack alert to #eng-security.
Anya (sec): agreed. Also let's document the minimal permission set and ensure build-sa follows least privilege: no owner/editor.
Devon (eng-infra): noted. I'll include the IAM diff and the PR link in the incident channel.
Anya (sec): thanks all. I'll write the short incident note and tag compliance. We'll close once we have the PRs merged and the preflight in CI. :white_check_mark:
